subject: Private deployment keystore stewardship — subprocessors & egress handling
messages:
From: Samir Patel <spatel@redmaplehealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Claudia Reyes <claudia.reyes@redmaplehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: keystore stewardship and subprocessor notification

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — RedMaple's security team asked me to follow up with a few concrete items we need to lock down before we move forward with a private VPC deployment:

1) Key ownership model: we need written confirmation of the supported approaches (BYOK + customer-managed HSM, Redwood-managed HSM with escrow, or hybrid).
2) Operator access: will Redwood engineers or subprocessors ever have access to unwrapped customer keys or PLAINTEXT data processed inside the instance? We need explicit, machine-actionable guarantees for our DPA and procurement team.
3) Subprocessor notification: provide the current list of subprocessors that would be involved for maintenance/patching/monitoring for an on-prem or VPC private deployment and the cadence for notification of changes.
4) Cross-border/egress: are there any conditions where telemetry or logs could be transferred outside the US? If so, we need details and opt-out mechanisms.

We are preparing a procurement SOW and need these items to align the DPA annex. Could you respond with a short statement for each item and any supporting artifacts (SOC2 excerpt, sample audit logs, or an example keystore-handshake playbook)?

Best,
Samir
Head of Security, RedMaple Health

---
Attachments: none listed

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <spatel@redmaplehealth.com>
Cc: Claudia Reyes <claudia.reyes@redmaplehealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: keystore stewardship and subprocessor notification

Hi Samir / Claudia,

Thanks — below are concise answers and I've attached two artifacts: a draft DPA keystore clause (for legal redlining) and our current subprocessor snapshot. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer to walk through.

1) Key ownership model:
- Supported modes: BYOK (customer provides wrapped keys/HSM-backed CMK), Customer-managed KMS (we integrate with your cloud KMS), and Redwood-hosted HSM with escrow. BYOK is the default recommended for the most restrictive environments.
- For BYOK we support both: a) customer-provisioned HSM/CMK and b) customer-supplied wrapped key material (we never store plaintext).

2) Operator access:
- Short answer: Redwood personnel and subprocessors do NOT have access to customer plaintext keys or unencrypted training/inference data under BYOK.
- Technical controls: we enforce KMS-only unwrap operations in a dedicated VPC subnet with strict IAM roles and per-instance service identities. Operator actions are restricted to operational playbooks that do not expose key material.
- Breakglass: in emergency cases we use an auditable 'breakglass' flow that requires two approvers from Redwood and one from the customer (detailed in the annex).

3) Subprocessor notification:
- Attached: subproc_list_snapshot_2028-04-12.csv with current vendors used for telemetry, managed patching, and HSM vendors.
- Cadence: quarterly update or immediate notification for high-risk changes. We will include contractually required notification windows in the DPA annex.

4) Cross-border / egress:
- Telemetry: aggregate telemetry (metrics, error rates) may be routed to Redwood regions for platform health; PII/data content is never exfiltrated.
- Logs: access logs and telemetry are kept within the region you select; by default US-only for this agreement. Any transfer will be subject to your prior consent.

I've attached the draft annex for your legal team to mark up. Proposed next steps:
- Legal redlines on the attached DPA annex (we can accept tracked changes)
- Short technical call to validate integration points (engineering + your security)
- DocuSign route once annex is agreed

Thanks — sending internal alignment note to our engineering and legal teams now (cc'ed).

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Privacy Programs, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments:
- draft_dpa_keystore_clause_v1.pdf (PDF, excerpt for keystore/escrow/breakglass)
- subproc_list_snapshot_2028-04-12.csv (CSV, current subprocessors)

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Re: Private deployment keystore stewardship — technical guardrails

Tessa / Marcus — quick notes from an ops/infra perspective (pulling from the attached draft):

- BYOK integration: prefer customer-managed CMK (cloud KMS) with Redwood only getting an encrypt/decrypt policy binding. For on-prem HSMs we support PKCS#11 wrapping; our agents perform unwrap operations in an isolated node that never logs key bytes.
- Operator access: we need to call out two technical constraints in the annex: (A) no ability to export unwrapped key material from the runtime, and (B) any maintenance requiring key exposure must use the 'customer-authorised breakglass' (two Redwood + one customer approver).
- Telemetry: redact request/response payloads at the platform edge before any metric shipping. Maintain a separate low-level health channel for token counts and latency only.

Proposed wording snippets for the annex (we can paste into the PDF):
- "Redwood will not access, copy, or persist plaintext customer key material in any supported BYOK configuration except via an auditable, customer-authorised breakglass process."
- "All operator actions are logged and retained for 7 years; customer may request a SOC2 evidence bundle on a quarterly basis."

I'll volunteer to join the technical call and can prepare a short runbook. Marcus, can you verify the HSM vendor list in the CSV matches supported FIPS levels?

-- Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Claudia Reyes <claudia.reyes@redmaplehealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <spatel@redmaplehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-14T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: keystore stewardship and subprocessor notification

Hi Tessa,

Thanks — that's helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from procurement/security that need explicit language in the annex:

1) Cross-border: you say logs are kept in-region by default. Can you add a clause guaranteeing no transfer of request/response payload content outside the contracted region without written consent? We need this for our DPA.
2) Escrow: if Redwood-hosted HSM with escrow is requested, will Redwood ever be able to reconstruct customer plaintext keys from the escrow material unilaterally? If yes, we need a mechanical escrow policy (split escrow / key shares).
3) Evidence: please provide the SOC2 subservice scope excerpt and an example audit bundle for the last 12 months so our auditors can review.

Also, please confirm the breakglass approval workflow and whether the request/approvers are recorded in audit logs we can retrieve.

If you can incorporate these into the annex and send a DocuSign-ready copy we'll start internal review.

Best,
Claudia
Director of Procurement, RedMaple Health

Attachments: none

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Claudia Reyes <claudia.reyes@redmaplehealth.com>, Samir Patel <spatel@redmaplehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-15T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment: keystore stewardship and subprocessor notification — annex and next steps

Claudia / Samir,

Thanks for the clear asks — we've incorporated language and artifacts as requested and attached the DPA annex for signature. Summary of agreed positions to be added to the annex:

• Region/egress: Redwood will not transfer request/response payloads outside the contracted region without prior written consent. Aggregate telemetry may be processed in Redwood regions for platform health; telemetry excludes customer payloads.
• Escrow policy: If Redwood-hosted escrow is elected, escrow uses a split-key model (Shamir-style share distribution) with at least two independent shares held by distinct Redwood personnel and one (optional) share custodied by a third-party escrow agent. Redwood cannot unilaterally reconstruct plaintext keys without the breakglass approvals described below.
• Breakglass: operational breakglass requires two authorised Redwood approvers and one authorised customer approver; every breakglass event is logged, tamper-evident, and available in the audit bundle.
• Evidence: attached SOC2 subservice excerpt and a sample audit bundle (redacted) — we'll provide a certified bundle under NDA if you need raw artifacts.

Attachments included for signing: dpa_annex_final_for_signing.pdf (DocuSign-ready). Links: HubSpot record and DocuSign envelope included in metadata.

Action items:
- RedMaple: review attached annex and provide redlines by EOD 2028-04-18 or confirm a 30-min legal call the same week.
- Redwood: Priyom to prepare runbook & audit evidence package; Marcus to validate HSM vendor FIPS level list; Tessa to route final DocuSign envelope by 4/16.

I'll route the DocuSign link after internal sign-off (expect 4/16). Let me know if you'd like a joint meeting — happy to set one.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Privacy Programs, Redwood Inference
